interface.title: ProteoClinView
interface.stage_of_work: Checking and interpreting results: confirming a protein's identity from its MS2 fragment ions
interface.what_it_is_for: A Streamlit app that computes theoretical c/z or b/y fragment ions for a demo or pasted protein sequence, matches them against a synthetic, bundled-mzML, uploaded-mzML or pasted MS2 peak list within a ppm tolerance, and reports coverage, a mirror plot and a per-ion mass-error table you can export.

data.note: I used all four spectrum sources. (1) The built-in synthetic demo spectrum, generated from the theoretical ions. (2) The bundled example example_data/insulin_b_chain_topdown.mzML, which has 1 MS2 scan (scan=2, RT=10.5, prec=608.28, 73 peaks). (3) The test file insulin_b_chain_topdown.mzML, uploaded through the Sequence Viewer sidebar (8.1 KB, 1 MS2 spectrum). (4) A hand-typed 5-peak list on the Mirror Plot. I used the three demo proteins (Human Insulin B chain, Human Ubiquitin, Hemoglobin α N-terminal) and also pasted the insulin B chain sequence (FVNQHLCGSHLVEALYLVCGERGFFYTPKT) myself. Possible mass offset: every singly charged N-terminal fragment the app computes is about +1.008 Da above the textbook value. For example, b1 of F is 149.0835 where 148.0757 is expected (screens/045.webp), b2 of FV is 248.1519 where 247.1441 is expected (screens/043.webp), and c1 is 166.1101 where 165.102 is expected (CSV). The reviewer confirmed this in the source (fragments.py:92,128): an extra H (1.007825) is added on top of the proton. The synthetic spectrum is built from the same calculation, so demo matches are not affected. This may be why the real mzML matches only 43/261 ions, though I did not confirm that.

features.name: Fragment-ion match settings with live summary metrics

features.specific: Sidebar c/z/b/y checkboxes, 'Maximum charge (z)' slider and 'Tolerance (ppm)' slider driving the 'Sequence length / Theoretical ions / Matched ions / Sequence coverage' metric row. Sequence coverage reads 100% whenever long c/z ions match (e.g. 87/116 on the demo), so it says little about how many cleavage sites are actually supported

screens_never_reached: Sequence coverage map (OpenMS-Insight SequenceView + LinePlot with StateManager cross-linking: 'click a residue to highlight the corresponding peak, click a peak to highlight the covered residues'). This is the README's headline Sequence Viewer component and the main intended way to see which residues are covered and link residues to peaks. It always failed with AttributeError: 'SequenceView' object has no attribute '_get_render_key', which looks like an openms-insight version mismatch (screens/007.webp, screens/008.webp). The Sequence Viewer had no annotated sequence map or spectrum plot in any state.

Everything on the Sequence Viewer below the crash (sequence_viewer.py:272, per the review), none of which rendered: the full theoretical fragment-ion table with 'Download as CSV' (proteoclinview_fragments.csv), the 'Supplementary: Plotly coverage map' expander (sequence_viewer.py:294-307), and the 'Mirror Plot ->' button that hands sequence, ion types and charges to the Mirror Plot (sequence_viewer.py:314-318).
FLASHTnT Search and Feature Map modules, listed as 'Planned' on Home, with no pages (screens/001.webp)
not_done: Could not view the annotated sequence coverage map or click a residue or peak to cross-highlight in the Sequence Viewer, because the component crashes as described above (screens/007.webp, screens/008.webp). This blocks the app's headline step of seeing which residues are covered and linking them to peaks. On that page only the summary metrics reflected ion type and charge changes.

Could not compare the real (bundled or uploaded) mzML in the Mirror Plot. Its spectrum source offers only 'Synthetic demo' and 'Paste peak list', with no mzML option, and the per-peak Δppm table for the mzML spectrum is only reachable through the broken Sequence Viewer. Matching a real spectrum therefore yielded only metric counts (43/261, screens/016.webp).

Settings did not carry from the Sequence Viewer to the Mirror Plot. The README's carry-over runs through the 'Mirror Plot ->' button below the coverage-map crash, which could not be reached, so I went through the sidebar nav. Each page then had its own sidebar at defaults (Insulin, c/z, z=2, 10 ppm), and '← Sequence Viewer' at the bottom of the Mirror Plot likewise returned to defaults (screens/028.webp, screens/049.webp, screens/050.webp). Per the review, even when settings do carry, the Mirror Plot's Demo protein mode ignores the carried sequence (mirror_plot.py:36).

Protein dropdown and metrics fell out of step: after switching from Human Ubiquitin back to Demo protein, the dropdown read 'Human Insulin B chain' while the metrics still showed Ubiquitin (76 AA) (check/screens/021.webp).
Clicking a legend entry did not visibly hide a trace (screens/032.webp). Hovering the '?' help icons showed no tooltip text (screens/044.webp).
The Mirror Plot caption 'At 10 ppm, a peak at m/z 500 matches … ±5.00 mDa' did not update when the tolerance moved to 1 or 50 ppm (screens/038.webp, screens/040.webp).
Did not open the exported PNG; only its download was confirmed (screens/054.webp).
